tasks.title: Read the verdict defensively
tasks.description:
In `src/verdict.ts`, implement `parseVerdict(text: string): Verdict`, returning `{ verdict, reason }` where `verdict` is `'pass'`, `'fail'` or `'unknown'`.

- A verdict label is the word `verdict` in any case, then optional spaces, `*` or `:`, then the whole word `pass` or `fail` in any case. `VERDICT: PASS` and `**Verdict:** fail` both count, wherever they appear in the text.
- If every verdict label in the text agrees, that is the verdict. If there is none, or two disagree, the verdict is `'unknown'`. Never read a verdict from a loose `pass` or `fail` elsewhere in the text.
- `reason`: for pass or fail, the rest of the line after a `reason` label written the same way, trimmed, or `''` when there is none. For unknown, a sentence that starts with `could not judge`.

The check runs hidden judge replies, some clean, some wrapped in extra words, some with no verdict at all.
nextSteps: Read the example judge replies in the lesson and decide which ones hold a clear verdict.
Write one regular expression for the verdict label and find every match.
Decide what to return for zero, one or several different matches.
Read the reason the same way.
hints: The judge's unclear replies contain the word "pass" in normal sentences. Only a label counts.
`text.matchAll(/\bverdict\b[\s*:]*.../gi)` finds every label. Put the lowercased words in a `Set` to see how many different verdicts there are.
A `Set` of size 1 is a verdict; any other size is unknown. For the reason, match `reason` the same way and capture `(.*)`, which stops at the end of the line.

tasks.title: Ask the judge, and know when it could not judge
tasks.description:
In `src/judge.ts`, implement `judgeDraft(ticket, draft, rubric, client = new OpenAI()): Promise<Verdict>`.

- Send `buildJudgeMessages(ticket, draft, rubric)` to `JUDGE_MODEL` with `temperature: 0`, and parse the reply with `parseVerdict`.
- If the verdict is unknown, ask once more: the same messages, then the judge's reply as an `assistant` message, then `FOLLOW_UP` as a `user` message.
- Never make more than 2 requests. If the second reply is still unclear, return its unknown verdict.
- If a request throws, return `{ verdict: 'unknown', reason }` where `reason` starts with `could not judge` and includes the error message.

Use the `client` parameter for every request; the check passes in fake clients.
nextSteps: Make the first request and parse it.
Return early when the verdict is pass or fail.
Build the follow-up conversation and ask once more.
Wrap the requests so an error becomes an unknown verdict.
hints: A small inner `ask(messages)` function that returns the reply text keeps the two requests short.
The follow-up is a conversation: the original messages, what the judge said, then your nudge. Spread the first array and add the two new messages.
One try/catch around both requests is enough. In the catch, build the reason from `(err as Error).message`.

tasks.title: Grade every draft
tasks.description:
In `src/judge.ts`, implement `evaluateDrafts(cases, rubric, client = new OpenAI()): Promise<DraftReport>`.

For each case, draft a reply with `draftReply(case.ticket, client)`, judge it with `judgeDraft`, and return:

- `results`: `{ id, draft, verdict, reason }` per case, in case order
- `pass`, `fail`, `unknown`: how many cases got each verdict
- `passRate`: `pass / (pass + fail)`, or `0` when nothing was judged

Unknown verdicts are reported, never counted as a pass or a fail. The check runs hidden tickets with the team rubric, and with a rubric that has a rule the judge cannot check.
nextSteps: Loop over the cases: draft, then judge.
Compute the pass rate from the judged cases only.
Run `node src/run.ts` and compare the two rubrics.
hints: Spread the verdict into the result: `{ id, draft, ...verdict }`.
A small `count(kind)` helper that filters the results keeps the three counts readable.
The denominator is `pass + fail`, not the number of cases. Guard it for zero.
